sections.name: AnchorSubjectType
sections.title: Kinds of anchored records
sections.what: Says the only kind of record that can be anchored right now is a verification result.
sections.why: Limiting the kinds keeps anchoring simple. Reason not stated in the code beyond this.
sections.watch_out: Adding a new kind here means updating every place that checks it.

sections.name: AnchorEvent
sections.title: Anchor event record
sections.what: Describes one stamped record: its id, the case it belongs to, what was stamped, its fingerprint, the fingerprint of the record before it, who signed it, and when.
sections.why: Linking each record to the one before it, through the previous fingerprint, makes the chain tamper-evident.
sections.watch_out: The previous fingerprint can be empty for the first record, so code must handle that case.

sections.name: PublicAnchorVerification
sections.title: Public check result
sections.what: Describes what an outside person sees when they check an anchor: whether it matches, the recomputed and stored fingerprints, who signed it, when, and the case reference.
sections.why: Gives outside checks a clear answer without exposing the internal record.
sections.watch_out: The recomputed fingerprint can be empty, so the display must handle a missing value.

summary: Defines the shape of a tamper-evident record that links a verification result to a signed hash.
purpose: Describes an anchor event, which is a stamped record of a verification result, and the public check result shown to outside people.
why: Anchors let someone confirm later that a result was not changed. Likely reason: this supports audit trust. Reason not stated in the code.
how: These are type labels only. Other code creates objects that must match these shapes.
inputs: None directly. Other code fills these shapes.
outputs: None directly. The shapes tell the checker what fields are expected.
risks: Changing a field name here can break code that reads anchors without a visible error until the app runs.
debug: If a check says a field is missing, compare the object with the matching type here.
